origin.usage: nchar_ctl(x, type = "chars", allowNA = FALSE, keepNA = NA, ctl = "all", warn = getOption("fansi.warn", TRUE), strip)

arguments.name: allowNA
arguments.text: Return NA for invalid UTF-8 instead of stopping.

arguments.name: keepNA
arguments.text: How a missing string is counted. NA selects the base nchar rule.

origin.details: type is chars, width, graphemes, or bytes, and a unique prefix is enough. Newlines are excluded unless ctl includes nl or omits all. A missing string is NA when keepNA is NA for chars and bytes, and 2 for width and graphemes.

translation.usage: nchar_ctl(x, type="chars", allowNA=False, keepNA=None, ctl="all", warn=None, strip=None)

arguments.name: allowNA
arguments.text: Return NA for invalid UTF-8 instead of stopping.

arguments.name: keepNA
arguments.text: How a missing string is counted. NA selects the base nchar rule.

translation.details: type is chars, width, graphemes, or bytes, and a unique prefix is enough. Newlines are excluded unless ctl includes nl or omits all. A missing string is NA when keepNA is NA for chars and bytes, and 2 for width and graphemes. A string is a length-one vector, and None is a missing string.
translation.example:
from fansi import nchar_ctl
print('nchar_ctl("\\033[31m123\\a\\r") returns %s.' % nchar_ctl("\x1b[31m123\a\r")[0])
